object: Practical knowledge that can only be acquired through experience in a particular place, time, and practice — James C. Scott's term (borrowed from Greek) for the local, embodied, tacit knowledge that high-modernist schemes systematically destroy.  The knowledge a farmer has of their particular field, a navigator of their particular coast, a craftsman of their particular material.
